title: Basic object-oriented programming
summary: Define a simple class with attributes and methods, and create multiple objects (instances) from it.
objectives: Define a class with the class keyword
Write a method that uses the object's own attributes
Create two independent objects from one class

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

So far your data has lived in separate variables, lists and dictionaries. A class lets you describe one kind of thing, such as a pet, together with the actions it can do. In this lab you will write a `Pet` class with an `__init__` method that stores a name and an age on `self`, plus an `introduce()` method that returns a sentence about that pet. You will then create two pets and print what each one says. Because each object keeps its own data, the two sentences will be different even though they come from the same class.

segments.title: Lab: a Pet class that introduces itself

lab.title: A Pet class that introduces itself
lab.objective: Write a class with two attributes and a method, then create two objects that each introduce themselves.
lab.instructions:
Define a class called Pet.

- __init__(self, name, age) stores name and age on self (self.name and self.age).
- introduce(self) returns (does not print) the text: I am <name> and I am <age> years old.

Then create two pets: rex = Pet("Rex", 3) and misty = Pet("Misty", 5). Print rex.introduce() on the first line and misty.introduce() on the second line.

Expected output:
I am Rex and I am 3 years old.
I am Misty and I am 5 years old.
lab.constraints: The class must be called Pet, with attributes name and age and a method introduce() that returns a string. Create objects with Pet(name, age). No input().
lab.starter_code:
# 1. Define the class Pet
#    - __init__(self, name, age): store name and age on self
#    - introduce(self): return "I am <name> and I am <age> years old."


# 2. Create two pets: rex = Pet("Rex", 3) and misty = Pet("Misty", 5)


# 3. Print rex.introduce(), then misty.introduce()
hints: Start with class Pet: and indent everything that belongs to it. The first method is def __init__(self, name, age): and inside it write self.name = name and self.age = age.
introduce is another def inside the class, with self as its only parameter. Build the sentence with an f-string using self.name and self.age, and return it instead of printing it.
Outside the class (no indentation) write rex = Pet("Rex", 3) and misty = Pet("Misty", 5), then print(rex.introduce()) and print(misty.introduce()).

visible_examples.description: A class with one attribute and one method
Two objects keep their own data
visible_examples.code:
class Counter:
    def __init__(self, start):
        self.value = start

a = Counter(1)
b = Counter(10)
print(a.value)
print(b.value)
